model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between coverage and the number of completions (k) for four different Llama model configurations: Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. The x-axis, labeled “Number of completions (k),” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 2⁰ (1) to 2⁸ (256), with tick marks at each power of two. The y-axis, labeled “Coverage,” is linear and spans from 0.4 to 0.8, with major gridlines at 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8. The Llama-3B line (solid blue with circle markers) starts at approximately 0.42 when k=1 and rises steadily to about 0.87 at k=256. The Llama-3B + FT line (dashed green with triangle markers) begins slightly higher at ~0.45 and reaches ~0.85 at k=256, showing a similar upward trend but slightly lower coverage than Llama-3B at higher k values. The Llama-1B line (solid light blue with square markers) starts at ~0.38 and climbs to ~0.82 at k=256. The Llama-1B + FT line (dashed light green with star markers) begins at ~0.40 and increases to ~0.80 at k=256, consistently tracking slightly below the Llama-1B line across the range. All lines exhibit a concave-down growth pattern, with coverage increasing more rapidly at lower k values and leveling off as k increases.
